description: Developed by solo computational researcher Team Hypernova, Ghost Telemetry is an interactive web-based archive and coordinate tracker designed to map, preserve, and tell the story of humanity’s off-world hardware left behind on the Moon and Mars.
summary:
Echoes Across Worlds: Five Silent Monuments is an interactive 3D cosmic storytelling web application and live NASA telemetry archive created by Aatiya Tasleem (Team Nadir-1) for learners ages 9–14 (grades 4–8).

To address the Abandoned But Not Forgotten challenge, the platform transforms historic spacecraft left on the Moon and Mars—the Apollo 11 Eagle Descent Stage, Apollo 15 Lunar Roving Vehicle, Apollo ALSEP Science Station, Opportunity Rover, and Ingenuity Mars Helicopter—from static museum artifacts into active, five-stage mission simulations. Students tune deep-space radio frequencies, resolve Apollo’s 1202 computer alarm, simulate Mars rotor aerodynamics, and analyze real NASA liftoff footage alongside live telemetry from NASA JPL Horizons, NSSDCA, NASA’s Image & Video Library, and NOAA DSCOVR.

This project matters because young learners connect far more deeply with space exploration when they experience real engineering challenges firsthand—bridging humanity’s historic planetary milestones with upcoming missions like Artemis, Mars Sample Return, and Dragonfly.
details:
What It Does & How It Works

Echoes Across Worlds: Five Silent Monuments is an interactive 3D cosmic storytelling and live NASA telemetry web application designed for learners ages 9–14 (grades 4–8). Rather than presenting space history as a static timeline, the platform guides users through a five-stage interactive mission flow for five iconic spacecraft resting on the Moon and Mars (Apollo 11 Eagle Descent Stage, Apollo 15 LRV-1 Rover, Apollo ALSEP Science Station, Opportunity Rover, and Ingenuity Mars Helicopter):

  1. Stage 1 — Deep Space Signal Tuner: Users tune into real MHz carrier frequencies to establish contact with each monument.
  2. Stage 2 — Mission Hardware & Challenges: Interactive engineering scenarios and quizzes test users on real historical crises (such as resolving Apollo 11's 1202 computer alarm).
  3. Stage 3 — NASA Liftoff & 2D Trajectory Simulator: Combines authentic archived NASA launch clips with an interactive trajectory launch simulation.
  4. Stage 4 — Interactive VR/2D Science Lab: Hands-on physics labs modeling lunar dust wheel traction, radioisotope power and moonquake telemetry, Martian dust-storm solar power drops, and supersonic rotor aerodynamics in Mars’ 1% atmosphere.
  5. Stage 5 — Final Transmission & Legacy Vault: Features a voice-reactive audio spectrum recreating poignant final transmissions before unlocking a vault connecting these pioneers to Artemis, Mars Sample Return, and Dragonfly.

Benefits & Intended Impact

  • Active STEM Engagement: Transforms passive reading into experiential problem-solving, helping middle-school students grasp complex aerospace physics, telemetry, and planetary science intuitively.
  • Bridging Past & Future: Demonstrates how engineering lessons from "abandoned" hardware directly enable humanity’s next era of deep-space exploration—inspiring young learners to see themselves as future scientists, engineers, and explorers.

Tools, Technologies & Open Space Data

  • Frontend & 3D Visualization: HTML5, CSS3, TypeScript/JavaScript, interactive 3D/2D canvas rendering, and Web Audio API for voice-reactive spectrum visualization.
    • NASA JPL Horizons Ephemeris (live planetary positions and distances)
    • NASA Image & Video Library API (archived mission footage and photography)
    • NASA NSSDCA Master Catalog (verified spacecraft specifications and landing coordinates)
    • NOAA DSCOVR Solar Wind (real-time interplanetary space weather telemetry)

Creativity & Key Design Considerations

  • Creative Storytelling Arc: Framing dormant spacecraft as "Five Silent Monuments" that still "speak" through live telemetry and historical transmissions blends emotional narrative with rigorous scientific simulation.
  • Human Factors Considered: Our team prioritized age-appropriate accessibility (clear visual feedback, audio narration, and step-by-step scaffolding for grades 4–8), scientific authenticity (grounding every mini-lab in real mission constraints), and universal web performance so any student can run the full 3D experience smoothly without specialized VR hardware.
